frs_sections.title: Scope and Purpose
frs_sections.content:
AFDX is built on top of standard IEEE 802.3 full-duplex switched Ethernet
but profiles and constrains that base technology to make it deterministic
and suitable for safety-critical avionics. Commercial off-the-shelf
Ethernet is non-deterministic: collisions, best-effort delivery, and
unbounded latency are unacceptable for aircraft control and display data.
AFDX adds a set of mechanisms on top of 802.3 — Virtual Links, Bandwidth
Allocation Gap, traffic shaping and policing, dual-network redundancy, and
Redundancy Management with Integrity Checking — that together turn
best-effort Ethernet into a deterministic, fault-tolerant network with
guaranteed bandwidth and bounded latency and jitter.

frs_sections.title: Determinism Built on Switched Ethernet
frs_sections.content:
The base layer is IEEE 802.3 full-duplex switched Ethernet. AFDX preserves
the standard Ethernet frame format (destination MAC address, source MAC
address, EtherType/length, payload, Frame Check Sequence (FCS)) so that
commercial Ethernet silicon and tooling can be reused, while adding the
deterministic profile on top.

Determinism is achieved through:
  - Virtual Links (VL) that segregate traffic into independent logical
    pipes with guaranteed bandwidth.
  - Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAG) traffic shaping that bounds the rate of
    each Virtual Link.
  - Jitter bounds at the End System transmit port.
  - Deterministic store-and-forward switching with per-VL policing in the
    switches.
  - Dual redundant networks (Network A and Network B) with Redundancy
    Management and Integrity C…

frs_sections.title: End Systems and Switches
frs_sections.content:
End System (ES):
The AFDX End System is the avionics network interface. It implements:
  - The MAC and physical layer (IEEE 802.3 full-duplex, typically
    100BASE-TX, 10/100 Mbit/s).
  - The Virtual Link transmit scheduler: per-VL traffic shaping enforcing
    the BAG and jitter, Sub-VL round-robin multiplexing, and the Virtual
    Link regulator.
  - Sequence Number insertion on transmit.
  - On the receive side: Integrity Checking per network and Redundancy
    Management (first-valid-wins de-duplication).
  - Replication of every transmitted frame onto Network A and Network B.

The avionics application communicates with the End System through
communication ports. AFDX defines two kinds of communication ports built on
UDP/IP:

frs_sections.title: AFDX Frame Format
frs_sections.content:
An AFDX frame is a standard IEEE 802.3 Ethernet frame, profiled as follows:

  - Destination MAC address (6 bytes): Constant Field (32 bits,
    0x03:00:00:00) + Virtual Link Identifier (16 bits). This is how the
    Virtual Link is carried on the wire and how switches forward.
  - Source MAC address (6 bytes): identifies the transmitting End System;
    structured as a constant field plus the network/equipment identifier of
    the source End System.
  - EtherType / Length (2 bytes): IP (0x0800).
  - Payload: IP header + UDP header + AFDX application payload. The AFDX
    application payload is 17 to 1471 bytes.
  - Sequence Number (1 byte): the AFDX redundancy Sequence Number, located
    after the payload and before the FCS. Range 1..255 (0 reserved).

frs_sections.title: Determinism Properties Summary
frs_sections.content:
- Guaranteed bandwidth per Virtual Link via the BAG (1..128 ms,
    power of two) and bounded Lmax: max bandwidth = Lmax / BAG.
  - Bounded latency: switches are store-and-forward with deterministic,
    bounded forwarding latency; the network is dimensioned offline so that
    worst-case end-to-end latency is bounded for every Virtual Link.
  - Bounded jitter at the End System output (e.g. ≤ 500 µs).
  - No congestion loss under the agreed traffic budget, enforced by transmit
    shaping (End System) and ingress policing (Switch).
  - Fault tolerance via dual networks (A/B), Sequence Number Integrity
    Checking, and first-valid-wins Redundancy Management.

These properties make AFDX a deterministic, redundant, profiled-Ethernet
avionics data network — ARINC 664 Part 7.

frs_sections.title: Configuration
frs_sections.content:
An AFDX network is statically configured offline. The configuration defines,
for every Virtual Link:
  - VL ID (16-bit Virtual Link Identifier).
  - BAG (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, or 128 ms).
  - Lmax and Lmin (maximum / minimum frame size).
  - The number of Sub-VLs (1 to 4).
  - The set of source and destination End Systems (the multicast tree).
  - The switch forwarding-table entries (VL ID → output ports) and the
    per-VL policing parameters at each switch.
  - Whether Redundancy Management is enabled for the Virtual Link.

This static configuration, together with the deterministic mechanisms above,
yields a network whose timing and bandwidth behaviour can be verified
offline for certification.

protocol_overview.type: Deterministic, redundant, profiled-Ethernet avionics data network (ARINC 664 Part 7 / AFDX). Built on IEEE 802.3 full-duplex switched Ethernet; adds Virtual Links, Bandwidth Allocation Gap traffic shaping, bounded jitter, and dual-network (A/B) redundancy with Sequence-Number Integrity Checking and first-valid-wins Redundancy Management.
protocol_overview.duplex: full-duplex point-to-point links (no shared medium, no collisions, no CSMA/CD); typically 100BASE-TX at 10/100 Mbit/s.
protocol_overview.encoding: PHY-class specific: 100BASE-TX uses 4B/5B then MLT-3; 100BASE-FX uses 4B/5B then NRZI; 1000BASE-T uses PAM5 with 8B1Q4 + Trellis coding; 1000BASE-X uses 8B/10B (same code as Fibre Channel / PCIe 1.x); 10BASE-T uses Manchester. MII/GMII/RGMII themselves carry plain LVTTL/LVCMOS nibble or byte data — encoding happens entirely inside the PHY.
interfaces_in_scope: Clause 4 — MAC frame format + CSMA/CD + full-duplex operation
Clause 22 — Reconciliation Sublayer (RS) + MII (10/100 Mb/s) + MDC/MDIO + Clause-22 management registers
Clause 45 — MMD-extended MDIO management (5-bit MMD + 16-bit register address per PHY)
Clause 28 — Auto-Negotiation (out-of-band Fast Link Pulse / Base Page exchange)
Clause 31 — MAC Control sublayer (PAUSE frame mechanism for full-duplex flow control)

frame_classes.Data_frame: Preamble + SFD + DA + SA + EtherType/Length + Payload + Pad + FCS
frame_classes.VLAN_tagged_frame: Preamble + SFD + DA + SA + VLAN tag (TPID 0x8100 + TCI) + EtherType/Length + Payload + Pad + FCS (max 1522 B)
frame_classes.PAUSE_frame: DA = 01:80:C2:00:00:01 (Slow Protocols Multicast) + SA + EtherType 0x8808 + Opcode 0x0001 + Pause Quanta (16b) + zero pad to 64 B + FCS
frame_classes.MDIO_C22_frame: PRE(32) + ST(01) + OP(read=10/write=01) + PHYAD(5) + REGAD(5) + TA(2) + DATA(16)
frame_classes.MDIO_C45_frame: PRE(32) + ST(00) + OP(addr=00/write=01/read=11/postRead=10) + PRTAD(5) + DEVAD(5) + TA(2) + DATA(16) — two-cycle protocol: address then read/write
frame_classes.Auto-Negotiation: 16-bit Base Page (Clause 28.2.1) advertised via Fast Link Pulse (FLP) bursts; encodes Selector / Tech Ability / Acknowledge / Remote Fault / Next Page

virtual_link.definition: Unidirectional logical connection from one source End System to one or more destination End Systems (point-to-point or point-to-multipoint / multicast).
virtual_link.id_location: carried in the Ethernet destination MAC address (constant field 0x03:00:00:00 + 16-bit VL ID)
virtual_link.sub_vl_note: Up to 4 Sub-VLs per VL, each with its own FIFO, round-robin multiplexed into the parent VL shaper; Sub-VLs share the parent BAG and do not appear on the wire.

bandwidth_allocation_gap.definition: Guaranteed minimum interval between the first bits of two consecutive frames on the same Virtual Link.

jitter.definition: Allowed variation of a frame's presentation time vs the ideal BAG-spaced instant at the End System output.
jitter.note: Bounded as a function of the Lmax values and link rate of the VLs sharing the physical port.

protocol_overview.traffic_shaping: Performed at the transmitting End System: regulates each VL to its BAG and jitter before frames enter the network.
protocol_overview.traffic_policing: Performed at the AFDX Switch ingress: polices each VL against its configured BAG and Lmax (token/leaky-bucket) and drops frames from a VL exceeding its allocation (babbling-source protection).

redundancy.scheme: Two physically independent networks; every frame replicated on both.
redundancy.integrity_checking: Per-network (A and B) check that each frame's Sequence Number is within the expected window for its VL; out-of-range frames rejected.
redundancy.redundancy_management: Merge the two streams first-valid-wins: the first correctly-received copy of a given Sequence Number is delivered; the duplicate is discarded; can be enabled/disabled per-VL.

protocol_overview.protocol_stack: Ethernet (AFDX) | IP (IPv4) | UDP | AFDX payload | Sequence Number | FCS

communication_ports.sampling: Holds a single message; a new message overwrites the previous one; reader gets the latest value plus a freshness/validity indication.
communication_ports.queuing: FIFO queue buffering multiple messages delivered in order without overwriting (lossless).

compliance_requirements: IEEE 802.3 full-duplex switched Ethernet base (no CSMA/CD).
Virtual Links with 16-bit VL ID in the destination MAC; up to 4 Sub-VLs per VL.
BAG ∈ {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128} ms with bounded jitter; transmit shaping + switch policing.
Dual independent networks A/B with per-frame replication.
1-byte Sequence Number, per-network Integrity Checking, first-valid-wins Redundancy Management.
Deterministic store-and-forward switches forwarding by VL ID with static configuration.
UDP/IP over the VL with sampling and queuing communication ports.
Offline static configuration enabling certification of timing and bandwidth.

functional_requirements.text: AFDX is built on IEEE 802.3 full-duplex switched Ethernet — point-to-point links, no shared medium, no collisions, no CSMA/CD — and preserves the standard Ethernet frame format.

Traffic is segregated into Virtual Links (VL): unidirectional logical connections from one source End System to one or more destinations, identified by a 16-bit Virtual Link Identifier carried in the destination MAC address.
A Virtual Link may be subdivided into up to four Sub-VLs, each with its own FIFO, round-robin multiplexed into the parent VL shaper; Sub-VLs share the parent BAG and are not visible on the wire.

Each VL has a Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAG), the guaranteed minimum interval between consecutive frames on that VL, a power of two from 1 to 128 ms; the maximum VL frame rate is 1/BAG and the maximum VL bandwidth is Lmax/BAG.
The End System bounds the transmit jitter on each VL (typically ≤ 500 µs), computed from the Lmax and link rate of the VLs sharing the physical port.
The transmitting End System shapes each VL to its BAG and jitter; the AFDX Switch polices each VL against its BAG/Lmax and drops non-conformant frames.
Two physically independent networks (Network A and Network B) are deployed; by default every frame is transmitted on both networks simultaneously.
A 1-byte Sequence Number is appended to every frame (after the payload, before the FCS), incrementing per frame on a VL and wrapping 255→1 (0 reserved).
Integrity Checking is performed independently on Network A and Network B: a frame whose Sequence Number is outside the expected window for its VL is rejected.

Redundancy Management merges the two redundant streams first-valid-wins: the first valid copy of a given Sequence Number is delivered and the duplicate discarded; RM can be enabled or disabled per VL.
AFDX Switches are deterministic store-and-forward switches that forward by VL ID using a static configuration table (no dynamic learning, no spanning tree) and police each VL.
UDP/IP (IPv4, with IP fragmentation) rides over the Virtual Link; UDP ports identify the End System's communication ports.
Two communication-port types are provided: sampling ports (single overwriting message with freshness indication) and queuing ports (FIFO, lossless).

error_response_conditions: Frame fails Ethernet FCS (CRC-32) — dropped at the receiver.
Sequence Number out of the expected window on a network — rejected as an Integrity Check error (per network).
Duplicate of an already-accepted Sequence Number — discarded by Redundancy Management (first-valid-wins).
VL exceeds its BAG/Lmax allocation at a switch — non-conformant frame policed (dropped).
One whole network (A or B) fails — redundancy delivers the surviving copy transparently.
Sampling-port data older than its validity timeout — flagged stale (not fresh) to the application.
